title: No Time for a Taxicab
description: Follow turn-by-turn navigation instructions on a city grid to locate Easter Bunny HQ.
writeup:
## Approach

The input is a sequence of navigation instructions like `R2` or `L3`. You begin at coordinate `(0,0)` facing North. Each instruction tells you to rotate 90° left or right, then walk forward a number of blocks.

Two tasks emerge:
- Track your final position after following all instructions
- Detect the first location you visit twice

To model movement, represent direction as an index (0=N, 1=E, 2=S, 3=W) and use simple `(dx, dy)` vectors for each cardinal direction.

## Part 1

Simulate the entire path:
- Update direction based on each turn
- Move forward the specified number of blocks
- Track your `(x, y)` position

After processing all instructions, compute the Manhattan distance from the origin:

```
abs(x) + abs(y)
```

This gives the shortest grid path to the final destination.

## Part 2

To find the first location visited twice, you must walk **one block at a time**, not jump entire distances.

- Maintain a `visited` set of coordinates
- For each step, check whether the coordinate has been seen before
- The first repeated coordinate is the answer

This incremental simulation ensures revisits are detected even when they occur mid‑instruction.

## Code Highlights

- Uses a direction index with `(dx, dy)` vectors for clean rotation logic
- Stepwise movement enables precise revisit detection
- A `set` provides O(1) membership checks for Part 2

The overall solution is a straightforward grid simulation with careful attention to movement granularity.
